subject: How to create custom legend for boxplot?

messages.author: 6ed2ff7838c0c40e
messages.subject: How to create custom legend for boxplot?
parts:
I have a grouped and faceted boxplot where the labels are self-explanatory so I don't need a legend for that. However, I'd like to add a legend showing which percentiles are represented by the boxes and whiskers.

To make this concrete, here is a ggplot boxplot where the box represents the 25th - 75th percentiles and the whiskers represent the 5th and 95th percentiles:

bp.pctiles <- function(x) {
  pctiles <- quantile(x, probs = c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95), na.rm=TRUE)
  names(pctiles) <- c("ymin", "lower", "middle", "upper", "ymax")
  pctiles
}

ggplot(mtcars, aes(cyl, mpg, group=cyl)) +
  stat_summary(fun.data=bp.pctiles, geom='boxplot',  colour='black') +
  facet_grid(am ~ . )

Now I'd like to add a legend on the right that looks something like the attached file. I made this with base graphics, but I'd like to create a generic boxplot (without any axes, background, etc.) that matches ggplot style and add it to the plot.

Thanks for any suggestions.

Joel

messages.subject: Re: How to create custom legend for boxplot?
parts:
Based on a suggestion from Dennis Murphy, I was able to get partway to a solution, but I'm still having some problems, as described below, and would appreciate suggestions on how to solve them.

The code below creates a boxplot and adds a grob intended to be the legend:

# Function for calculating boxplot percentiles in stat_summary
bp.pctiles <- function(x) {
  r <- quantile(x, probs = c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95), na.rm=TRUE)
  names(r) <- c("ymin", "lower", "middle", "upper", "ymax")
  r
}

# Data frame of random normal values for plotting as a boxplot
set.seed(10)
bpd = data.frame(values=rnorm(100))

# Data frame of quantiles of the values above. This will actually be used only for labeling the boxplot using geom_text
qntiles = data.frame(quantiles = quantile(bpd$values, probs=c(0.05,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.95)))
qntiles$pctiles = c('5th','25th','50th','75th', '95th')
qntiles$x = c(0.74,rep(0.19,3),0.70)

# Create the boxplot that will become the legend. This is a boxplot with all elements blank except
# the boxplot and its percentile labels
bp_legend = ggplot(bpd, aes(x=" ",  y=values)) +
   stat_summary(fun.data=bp.pctiles, geom='boxplot', position='dodge', colour='blue', lwd=.9) +
  theme(panel.background=element_blank(),
        axis.line=element_blank(),
        text=element_blank(),
        axis.ticks=element_blank()) +
  geom_text(data=qntiles, aes(x=x, y=quantiles, label=pctiles), size=10) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim=c(-.1,1.5))

# Add legend to boxplot
# First create the boxplot
bp_plot = bpggplot(mtcars, aes(cyl, mpg, group=cyl)) +

facet_grid(am ~ . ) +
  theme(plot.margin=unit(c(1,4,1,1),'lines')) # Create right margin for legend

# Add bp_legend to the boxplot
bp_plot + annotation_custom(grob=ggplotGrob(bp_legend), ymin=15,ymax=35,xmin=7.5, xmax=9)

If you run the code, you'll see a few problems. First, the legend is inside the plot, rather than in the right margin, because I haven't figured out how to access the margin area around the plot, rather than the plot itself. Second, ggplot puts the legend inside every facet, but I want only one legend for all the facets. Third, the graphic is distorted, with the text too large, clipped, and overlapping the boxplot. Furthermore, the relative size and location of the text depends on the dimensions I choose in annotation_custom. I can save bp_legend as a png or svg (see code below) and it looks exactly the way I want. But how do I create a grob of bp_legend that looks just like the png or svg files I was able to create?

png("bp_legend.png", width=200, height=800)
bp_legend
dev.off()

svg(file="bp_legend.svg", width=3, height=12)
bp_legend
dev.off()

Thanks for any suggestions on how to address these issues.

Joel
